newsitem.title: USA: Excel, Swift to reduce U.S. hog slaughter.
newsitem.headline: Excel, Swift to reduce U.S. hog slaughter.

text.p: Excel Corp and Swift and Co said Friday they will scale back hog slaughter next week in reaction to poor returns on pork.
The news follows IBP Inc's announcment Thursday that it cut production at five of its seven pork plants this week and will operate at reduced capacity next week.

Excel, a division of Cargill Inc, will reduce production next week at its hog plants, said Excel spokesman Mark Klein. No details were provided regarding the extent of the reduction or when production would return to normal.
Excel's three hog slaughter plants are in Beardstown, Ill., Marshall, Mo., and Ottumwa, Iowa.
"Swift and Co is cutting back all its pork plants to seven hours of production until further notice. There will be no Saturday operations," that company said in a statement.

Swift, a subsidiary of ConAgra Inc, blamed inadequate returns for the cutbacks. The company's three plants have a daily slaughter capacity of 38,000 head and each normally operates eight hours a day, said David Heggestad, Swift president.
Its plants are located in Worthington, Minn., Marshalltown, Iowa, and Louisville, Ky.
